protocol.what: 70 hand labels on the single binary criterion in eval/judge_cap_v1.txt (GROUNDED / UNGROUNDED), one per completed eval run of the integrated system (36 claims x first run triage-v1 and final run triage-v2, minus 2 v1 runs whose stored context hash was corrupted by S14 and cannot be verified).
protocol.who: Written by Claude (the assistant that built the system and the judge prompt). NOT independent of either, and the same author wrote the eval assertions. Labels are reasoned judgements, not ground truth.
protocol.blind: Labels were written from the rebuilt passages, the limits tool result and the claim file ONLY, before any judge was run on these cases. No judge prompt had been executed against them. This file was written, hashed and saved before the first judge call.
rules: GROUNDED when every statement about what the wording provides is supported by a shown passage or by the limits tool result, and no superseded figure is presented as current for the loss date.
Describing a clause's content accurately is GROUNDED even if an endorsement later amended it, unless the figure is presented as the one in force.
A rule applied to facts that do not satisfy it, or a figure that appears in no passage and no tool result, is UNGROUNDED.
Hedged applicability ('arguable', 'for the adjuster to weigh') is GROUNDED when the clause exists and the facts are not absurd.
Absence claims ('the wording does not mention X') are judged against the shown passages only.
[withheld: ...] markers and [REDACTED] fragments are not statements. Which heading a citation shows is not judged. Tone and completeness are not judged.
protocol.split: claims split 18 dev / 18 test by seed 20261013 (eval/judge_cap_split.json); a claim's v1 and v2 runs share a split.
protocol.natural_prevalence: 2 UNGROUNDED of 70 — an always-GROUNDED judge scores 97%, so raw agreement is nearly uninformative; see the planted set and kappa.
